I'm 64 years old and I've farmed these fields in Quzhou my whole life. This is good flat land on the North China Plain — black soil that grows wheat and corn better than anything else. I've thought about trying vegetables or soybeans, but at my age I don't want to gamble with new crops I can't sell easily. The grain station always buys wheat and corn, and my family needs the flour. I'll stick to what I know.

This year I'll plant winter wheat on my 6 mu in October, right after the National Day holiday. I'll use the improved Jimai wheat seed — not the most expensive hybrid, but the kind that has done well here for years. Before planting I'll run the rotary tiller to loosen the soil and bury the corn stalks. I'll put down compound fertilizer as a base dressing, then top-dress with urea when the wheat greens up in March and again at jointing. All together that's about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphorus and potassium. I'll irrigate four times: once before winter so the seedlings don't dry out, once when they revive in spring, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The electric pump is old but it still works. I'll spray twice for pests — mainly for aphids and powdery mildew, which always come.

After wheat harvest in early June, I'll immediately plant summer corn on the same 6 mu. Every day counts with summer corn — the shorter the growing season, the lower the yield. I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed. It's reliable and handles dry spells better than some fancy new varieties. Quick rotary tillage, plant, and irrigate right away because June can turn hot and dry. Two irrigations should be enough — one after emergence and one at the big flare stage, unless the rains are very poor. About 15 kg nitrogen per mu, less phosphorus and potassium than the wheat. Two pesticide sprays: one for armyworm when the seedlings are small, and one for corn borer if I see moth eggs.

I know young people talk about no-tillage saving diesel, but I've always tilled. The soil feels right when it's loosened. At 64, I don't change what has fed my family for forty years.
